context.text: Small portions of hydrochloric acid at room temperature are added to a fixed amount of sodium hydroxide solution. The mixture warms. The schematic shows temperature against total acid volume; heat of dilution is neglected.
Explain the maximum and why further acid addition lowers the temperature.

context.alt: Temperature rises with acid addition to a maximum, then falls as more acid is added.

prompt.text: At the maximum, what has happened to the alkali?

accepted: all the sodium hydroxide has reacted

prompt.text: After the maximum, why does adding more acid lower the temperature?

accepted: Cooler acid is added and no further neutralisation occurs
no further neutralisation and the cooler acid cools the mixture
the alkali is used up and cooler acid lowers the temperature
cooler acid dilutes the hot mixture after neutralisation is complete

workedAnswer.text: Cooler acid is added and no further neutralisation occurs
The alkali has been consumed. Further cooler acid lowers the mixture temperature; the fall does not mean neutralisation has become endothermic.

context.text:
A fuel burns and heats water in an aluminium can.
The measured heat energy released per gram of fuel is lower than expected.
Apart from heat loss to the surroundings, identify the most likely error and explain its effect on the heat energy released.

accepted: the fuel does not burn completely

prompt.text: Compared with complete combustion of the same mass of fuel...

options.id: The same heat energy is released, but the thermometer cannot detect it.

content.text: The same heat energy is released, but the thermometer cannot detect it.
More heat energy is released.
Less heat energy is released.
No heat energy is released.

workedAnswer.text: Incomplete combustion is one possible error. The fuel is not fully oxidised.
Incomplete combustion releases less heat energy per gram of fuel than complete combustion. This is a reduction in energy released, separate from energy subsequently lost to the surroundings.
